---
title: "Outline"
---

The SCOW API serves a reform as ordered *blocks* (`orden`, `numero`,
`referencia`, `contenido`, `tamanio`). The writer puts one marker line before
each block that yields text:

```text
<!-- scjn:block orden=N numero=N kind=<kind> [type=] [num=] label="..." -->
```

## The kinds

`kind` is one of `header`, `recitals`, `preamble`, `toc`, `transitorios`,
`decree`, `container`, `article`, `provision`, `other`.

## The guarantees

- The marker is an HTML comment on purpose: no character of the text changes.
  `strip_markers` returns the text byte for byte, and
  `markdown_de_snapshot(..., outline=False)` is the text without markers.
- Every block that yields text has exactly one marker.
- A block that yields none (an editorial `N. DE E.` aside) leaves its `orden` as
  a gap that the raw answer explains.
- A marker is metadata, never embedded in the text.

`md2akn` reads the markers; it imports nothing from `scjn`, and the two are tied
by a generated vocabulary fixture rather than by an import.

## Raw answers are kept

Every reform's answer is stored gzipped under `scripts/scjn/raw-api/`, so the
writer can change without a re-crawl (`scripts/rewrite_scjn_from_raw.py`).

## The completeness guard

An answer is complete when its `orden` values are exactly `1..max` and it
carries at least `tamanio` rows. An incomplete answer is requested again and
then refused with `ScjnApiIncompleteError`, so the reform counts as failed and no
file is written. A verbatim repeated row is dropped, first kept; two *different*
blocks sharing an `orden` both stay. An instrument is swapped in whole or not at
all.

## Tables

A tab-bearing block is a table: a blank line ends a row, a bare newline is a
wrapped line inside a cell, a run of tabs separates columns. One recovered row is
one Markdown paragraph `| cell | cell |`, with no header separator, and an
`Artículo N` lead on a tabbed line is never a row. The lead of an article is
bolded whole (`**Artículo 1.1**:`).

## Verifying it

`scripts/verify_scjn_outline.py` checks the contract over the local corpora and
their raw answers, read-only and with no network:

- **writer drift**: the body rebuilt from the raw answer against the body on disk;
- **marker completeness**: every raw block with text has exactly one marker;
- **attribute round-trip**: each marker equals `marker_line(parse_marker(...))`;
- **text invariance**: `strip_markers` of the rebuilt body is the `outline=False` text.

It exits with 1 only on a round-trip or invariance violation.
`scripts/measure_block_gaps.py` counts the snapshots whose `orden` markers have a
gap and which of them are explained.
